data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Tarci', meaning 'help'. This name was borne by St. Tarcisius, a boy martyred during the persecution of Christians in ancient Rome. The name Tarcisia carries the meaning “Helpful, ready to help” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tarcisia usually hope their child will grow to embody helpful, ready to help and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Tarcisius, a Roman boy who died a martyr's death during the persecutions under Emperor Alaric the Visigoth in 410 AD, is believed to have been carrying the Eucharist for the Pope when he was captured and killed. His relics are now venerated in the Church of San Crispino and San Giuliano in Rome.
historical_references.context: During the Roman Empire, there were numerous persecutions against Christians. Alaric the Visigoth, a Germanic king, attacked Rome and led to the sack of the city. Tarcisius, a young deacon, was martyred while trying to protect the Eucharist from falling into the hands of the looters.

historical_references.reference: Another legend surrounding Tarcisius tells of him being a young boy during the persecutions under Emperor Decius around 250 AD. He was caught attending a clandestine Christian ceremony and was ordered to renounce his faith. When he refused, he was tortured and eventually killed. His relics were later discovered and venerated in the Basilica di San Crispino e San Giuliano in Rome.
historical_references.context: During the early Christian period, there were numerous emperors who persecuted Christians due to their refusal to worship the Roman gods. Emperor Decius issued an edict requiring all citizens to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods. Tarcisius, a young boy, was caught attending a Christian ceremony and was martyred for his faith.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name Tarcisia has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts, primarily within the Catholic community. The name has been associated with Catholicism, nuns, and education. On social media platforms, there are numerous accounts and groups dedicated to the study and celebration of Catholic saints, including Tarcisia. In literature, there have been recent publications featuring characters named Tarcisia, often portrayed as Catholic nuns or women of faith. Lastly, in film, there have been productions that include a character named Tarcisia, such as the independent film 'The Nun's Story' (1959) starring Audrey Hepburn. Overall, the name Tarcisia represents a strong connection to Catholicism, spirituality, and education.
